ideas.title: Stipple-map of single-cell AP-1 history (dappled lineage tracing)
ideas.description: Use a FOS/JUN knock-in fluorescent or recombinase-based reporter (e.g., Fos-CreER-style tagging) to permanently mark cells that experienced a stimulus, then follow the marked and unmarked 'dappled' mosaic through divisions. Re-challenge and compare transcriptional response and chromatin state between marked and unmarked sister lineages to test whether past AP-1 activity predicts altered future responses.

ideas.title: Paired-stimulus priming with washout time course
ideas.description: Expose cells to a first AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or wounding), wash out, and re-stimulate after variable delays (hours to many cell divisions). Measure the second-response magnitude by RNA-seq and nascent transcription, and test whether AP-1 dose, delay, and motif-linked gene sets quantitatively predict memory duration, using JUN/FOS dominant-negative (A-FOS) to show necessity.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome of AP-1 motif accessibility persistence
ideas.description: Run scATAC+RNA-seq before, during, and long after stimulation. Track whether AP-1-motif (chromVAR) accessible regions stay open after AP-1 protein levels return to baseline, and whether this heterogeneity (fast/slow, sweet/sour-like cell states) maps onto subsequent responsiveness at the single-cell level.

ideas.title: Acute degradation to separate initiation from maintenance
ideas.description: Tag endogenous AP-1 factors (JUN, FOSL, BATF) with a degron and deplete them either during the priming stimulus or only after the memory state has formed. If memory sites (ChIP/CUT&RUN, ATAC, H3K27ac) persist and the enhanced response remains after AP-1 loss at later times, AP-1 is only an initiator. If memory decays, AP-1 is required for maintenance.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 enhancer perturbation and live reporting
ideas.description: Use CRISPR dCas9 tools to edit or mutate specific AP-1 motifs at memory-associated enhancers (CRISPRi or base editing), while using live-cell imaging of a reporter at the locus. Test whether the motif is causally needed for faster or stronger reactivation after a prior stimulus, and whether ectopic AP-1 motifs can install memory at a naive locus.
